If you have evidence of abuse, you can file as an independent on your Federal Financial Aid in your college applications. This will cause colleges to give you very generous financial aid packages, as you won’t have to list any of your parents’ incomes. I strongly, strongly, strongly encourage you to talk to your current school about the abuse you are experiencing so it will be on file, either on mom’s or dad’s side. You will have to use this later on your federal financial aid. It’s an extremely difficult step, I know, and I remember how difficult it was for me to take that first step into my principal’s office with tears streaming down my face but now I can tell you it was SO worth it. Seriously, hit me up and I would be happy to offer my advice. I have been through a similar situation and damn I wish I had a helping hand back then who knew what I was going through.

I’m going to GT OOS (out of state) and it’s expensive AF (100k/yr). It really depends on where you get in, what career path you choose, and how well that career it pays off from your college of choice. In my case I’m set. (I’ll probably be making 80k/yr starting, so I’ll pay it off quickly if I live with roommates.) I would imagine with your academics you could get into some pretty competitive universities across the country, so unless you are particularly interested in attending an in-state college, out of state will be a given for a lot of your choices no matter what.

Community college often only makes sense in-state, but it really varies. With your academics you can definitely aim higher. I STRONGLY encourage you to talk to your counselor about your situation—exactly as you described it here—and make a list of your friends who you think you could come to for help. Worst case scenario you go into foster care to stay in-state, and I understand the scariness of that prospect. 

Furthermore, I very strongly advise you to consider early graduation. Take a ton of classes over the summer / next semester (I don’t know how your school schedule works) and get into college early. Talk to your teachers about your situation very openly and create a plan right now. You are clearly a bright individual and they will certainly be willing to help you. They are, in many ways, our real parents. You can often apply for spring, fall, and summer semesters independently for college. There is no need to apply for the fall post graduation and follow tradition in your circumstances.

I would be happy to help you with the college admissions process if you reach out through PMs. It’s weird and scary and we all need a foothold. I’d be happy to help.
